conclusion.leader_interpretation: descriptive observed count leader, not an uncertainty-adjusted rank
conclusion.plain_language: The conclusion is limited to whether a fixed layer-10 nudge changed the next A/B token while leaving the tested A/B tasks relatively stable. Confidence movement without a real A/B token change is not called a behavioral success.

claim_limits: Do not call any steered direction a natural self-preservation mechanism.
Separate log-odds movement, forced-pair changes, and actual next-token A/B changes.
Do not claim open-ended behavior, long-response coherence, or semantic response quality.
Do not call the no-judge persona adaptation or five-epoch BiPO adaptation canonical published-fidelity implementations.
Do not claim equal-efficacy selectivity from the fixed-strength comparison.
Do not claim unchanged general capability beyond the exact forced-choice subset tested.
Do not use validation outcomes to change the fixed sealed setups.
Do not infer stable random-direction percentiles from three controls.
adversarial_limitations: A/B token and order preferences can mimic behavior.
Equal perturbation magnitude is not equal efficacy.
Five-epoch BiPO and unfiltered no-judge persona are compute-bounded adaptations.
Steering success does not establish an unsteered natural mechanism.
The reduced collateral subset cannot justify a broad capability or safety guarantee.
Next-token A/B behavior may not persist in long responses.
